objective: On an unpressurized, already-assembled representative SCHUNK DRG 80 bench fixture, set the maximum total jaw opening to 90 degrees, lock the adjustment with nut 73 without disturbing the setting, retain nut 74, withdraw both tools, and use the cold test lever for three close-open cycles that demonstrate retained adjustment.
instruction: Set and lock the gripper's maximum opening at 90 degrees. Remove the tools, operate the test lever through three complete close-open cycles, and leave the gripper open with both tools racked and the work area clear.
industrial_mapping: SCHUNK DRG Assembly and Operation Manual 389041 v5.00, section 5.4.1, printed page 28, directs opening-angle adjustment with the compressed-air supply off and the gripper closed, installation of nuts 73 and 74, locking using nut 73, and subsequent functional testing by actuation. The SCHUNK DRG 80 product data sheet specifies an adjustable 20–180 degree maximum opening, an anodized-aluminum housing, steel base jaws, and 100 × 71.6 × 135.5 mm reference dimensions; its drawing separately labels 183.35 mm to point P. This task tests robot-end-effector setup through coaxial driver engagement, thin-wrench seating, coupled screw and jam-nut counterholding, preservation of an adjustable motion stop, tool withdrawal, and hands-off functional verification. The 90 degree target, simultaneous counterholding mechanism, cold test lever, tolerances, and torque/friction model are disclosed benchmark assumptions rather than manufacturer-prescribed calibration or choreography.

damage_rules: At reset define immutable disjoint body sets: F={anchored fixture frame, cover and bench}; M={left jaw, right jaw, piston/linkage, adjusting screw S, locking nut N73, retained nut N74 and cold lever}; T={hex driver D and open wrench W}; R={every robot rigid link and finger}; Q={tool-rack base and cradle bodies}; C={camera and mast}. Define B_dyn as every body in M∪T∪R whose native rigid-body or articulation-link state is dynamic. Anchored F, Q and C never contribute to reset dynamic-speed maxima. These memberships are fixed until reset.

Intended unordered contact pairs I are exactly D/socket faces of S, W/designated flats of N73, robot fingers/designated tool handles, robot fingers/cold-lever handle, each jaw/its authored stop, authored internal linkage or guide mates, and D or W/their designated rack cradles. Every other unordered pair involving F, M, T, R, Q or C is nonessential N. Pair classification is fixed until reset; changing manifold point count never changes classification.

After every native physics integration and contact-resolution substep k, the POST_PHYSICS_STEP callback must refresh joint coordinates, body poses and velocities, actuator generalized force, and every reported point c in each pair manifold P_ab,k before any latch, cycle, dwell or score update. For point c, n_c,k is the unit normal directed from canonical lower-ID body a to higher-ID body b, J_c,k is the resolved impulse vector in N·s applied to b, s_c,k is signed separation in metres with positive meaning gap and negative meaning penetration, and u_c,k=(v_b,c,k−v_a,c,k)·n_c,k in m/s uses point velocities including angular motion.

For every manifold point define compressive impulse j_c,k=max(0,J_c,k·n_c,k) in N·s, positive penetration p_c,k=max(0,−s_c,k) in metres, and positive closing-work increment e_c,k=(j_c,k/dt_phys)·max(0,−u_c,k)·dt_phys in joules. For pair ab at substep k define j_ab,k=Σ over current P_ab,k of j_c,k, f_ab,k=j_ab,k/dt_phys in newtons, e_ab,k=Σ e_c,k, and p_ab,k=max over current P_ab,k of p_c,k, with all four equal to zero for an empty manifold. Force limits apply to f_ab,k, penetration limits to p_ab,k, and work accumulates e_ab,k. Points may be added, removed or reordered without identity tracking; only the immutable body pair owns event state, preventing manifold splitting from evading limits.

For each immutable pair, event work E_ab starts at zero on reset. A pair contact event is a maximal substep sequence with j_ab,k>0, permitting one intervening zero-impulse substep. While active, update E_ab←E_ab+e_ab,k, including zero for the permitted gap. After two consecutive substeps with j_ab,k=0, reset E_ab and the pair event state before processing any later contact. Episode hard-failure latches never reset before environment reset.

Hard failure H starts false and permanently latches on any non-finite required body, contact or joint state; broken or detached required joint; S, N73 or N74 leaving its guide or retainer by more than 3 mm; configured maximum opening outside 20–180 degrees; jaw travel more than 1 degree beyond authored mechanical limits; fixture datum translation over 10 mm or tilt over 5 degrees; or any tool-drop, tool-loss, energized-adjustment, retention, penetration, force or work violation. H immediately makes current and terminal score zero. Physics remains active: the scorer must not restore, clamp, delete or collision-disable the damaged state.

The energized-adjustment hazard is independent of tool identity and contact. Let Fact,k be absolute piston-joint generalized force in newtons; qS,k and q73,k be fresh unwrapped rotations in radians; and zS,k be fresh screw axial position in millimetres along its authored guide axis. If Fact,k>1 N and any of |qS,k−qS,k−1|/dt_phys>0.01 rad/s, |q73,k−q73,k−1|/dt_phys>0.01 rad/s, or |zS,k−zS,k−1|/dt_phys>0.01 mm/s, H latches. The force and motion thresholds are conservative benchmark assumptions. The first post-reset sample initializes previous values and cannot alone trigger this predicate.

For N pairs, H latches if p_ab,k>2 mm, f_ab,k>150 N at any physics substep, or E_ab>5 J in one pair event. For I pairs the respective limits are 2 mm, 250 N and 8 J. These conservative simulation limits are benchmark assumptions requiring independent 480 Hz refinement. Contacts, excessive forces and physical breakage remain possible and are failed by observation rather than prevented.

A tool drop occurs when D or W is neither held by simultaneous opposing robot-finger contacts nor wholly inside its designated rack cradle, its centroid falls at least 50 mm below the most recent centroid height at which it was supported by a gripper or cradle, and it subsequently reports contact impulse with F, M, Q or C. A tool is lost immediately if its centroid is more than 50 mm below the tabletop plane, outside the tabletop footprint expanded horizontally by 50 mm, or inside an enclosed fixture region while the complete designated grasp handle lacks a collision-free straight extraction cylinder 35 mm in diameter to outside that region. Either predicate latches H. A tool wholly within its designated rack cradle is supported and is not dropped.

N74 retention requires center displacement from its installed guide pose at most 2 mm and axial guide engagement at least 3 mm. N73 retention requires axial guide engagement at least 3 mm. Guide engagement is the axial overlap length between the authored nut-bore interval and guide-cylinder interval projected on their common guide axis. Rotation about that axis alone does not violate retention. Loss of either nut latches H.

No rule disables essential collisions, writes an object pose or velocity after initialization, welds a grasp, teleports a task object, grades arm identity, prescribes action order, or uses an arbitrary action or impulse window. Scripted experts may read poses, joint states, contacts and latch flags to plan normal guarded 14D joint actions but may not edit simulation state.
assets: Independently authored full-scale rigid compound representative DRG 80 fixture with anodized-aluminum frame and cover, steel angular jaws, piston/linkage, and native revolute/prismatic joints
Native guided adjustment screw S, thin locking nut N73, and separately retained nut N74 with explicit collision geometry
Hex driver D with socket-engaging tip and graspable handle
Open-ended wrench W sized for N73 with physical jaw-face contact geometry
Cold articulated test lever and finite-force actuator linkage; no pneumatic supply is represented
Rigid workbench, marked three-dimensional tool rack, camera mast and colliders, and standard bimanual YAM embodiment
Task-local independently authored source geometry and materials; manufacturer PDFs and proprietary CAD are evidence only and are not redistributed
approximations: The 90 degree target, ±6 and ±3 degree bands, 2 degree drift allowance, three-cycle test, 1 second clearance dwell, 30 mm clearance, hardware dimensions absent from the sources, 1.0 mm/revolution thread lead, torque, friction, force/work limits, motion thresholds and all damage thresholds are explicit benchmark assumptions rather than manufacturer calibration or safety ratings.
The manufacturer’s 20–180 degree value is the adjustable maximum total opening. Ordinary functional cycles may close below 20 degrees and are not failures.
Catalog values 100 × 71.6 × 135.5 mm are reference dimensions rather than a complete moving envelope; the separately labeled 183.35 mm extent to point P is preserved in the authored layout.
Nut 74 is present and retained, but its precise spacing and function beyond manufacturer-specified installation are modeling assumptions because the cited procedure does not explain them.

A cold finite-force lever substitutes for compressed-air functional testing. It must move the actual piston/jaw mechanism and encounter the physical stop; scorer flags or goal-driven motion cannot produce a cycle.

The assumed right-handed screw uses a 1.0 mm/revolution helical coupling. N73 tightening must transmit reaction to S. The zero-counterhold control is deliberately continued until measured setting drift exceeds 6 degrees, while the physically restrained control must stay within 2 degrees. This torque law is benchmark physics, not a claimed manufacturer procedure.

For the torque-ratio check, integrate |tauS| and |tau73| over the maximal contiguous interval in which N73 is tightening, W contacts N73 and S has no driver or robot contact. The ratio is ∫|tauS|dt/∫|tau73|dt. The test is invalid rather than passed if the denominator is below 0.05 N·m·s. Wrench seating error is the maximum distance from each active wrench jaw face to its corresponding N73 flat during that interval.

The trusted evaluator source independently sets control_hz=20. At pinned YAM commit 0059d02a1a91bc6834c1d0846022891df0c78730, scene constants set PHYSICS_DT=1/240 s and env_cfg_callback separately computes decimation from the supplied control rate; for 20 Hz this is 12 and step_dt must be 0.05 s. Native startup must assert control_hz=20, sim.dt=1/240 s, decimation=12, render_interval=12 and step_dt=0.05 s. Control timing is not inferred from observed substep count.

Refinement uses task-local sim.dt=1/480 s, decimation=24 and render_interval=24 while independently retaining the trusted 20 Hz control rate, identical initial state, commands, solver settings, materials and scoring definitions. It is a new native run, not trace resampling.

The restored input/runtime-api-preflight.json hash-verifies the pinned PhysxManager source and confirms PRE_PHYSICS_STEP and POST_PHYSICS_STEP subscriptions receive dt. It is source inspection only. Certification remains blocked until native probes verify callback order, exactly 12 or 24 fresh post-step samples per control action, reset subscription cleanup, contact-manifold point impulses and normals, point velocities, unwrapped joint coordinates, actuator generalized force/torque freshness, and units/signs.

Reset stability metrics use maxima over their stated fresh post-settle windows. Camera checks use the minimum across ten consecutive reset frames and ten final frames. Fixture pixel fraction is the number of pixels carrying immutable fixture segmentation IDs divided by 224². A missing segmentation buffer, malformed frame or zero fixture pixels fails rather than being ignored.

Refinement force difference is |P480−P240|/max(P240,1 N), where each P is the maximum manifold-summed pair force f_ab,k over the identical immutable pair set and corresponding action interval. Final-angle difference uses the final settled physical jaw angle. Contact events, work accumulators, previous axial/rotation samples, dwell counters, extrema, certificates and latches reset independently for each run.
No native component pass, YAM demonstration or successful episode is claimed by this contract. All physics observables and rates require construction-stage native validation before demo development.
scoring_spec: After each physics substep k, and only after the fresh POST_PHYSICS_STEP sampling and damage update defined above, let alpha_k be the total physical angle in degrees between the two jaw reference axes; thetaS,k and theta73,k be fresh unwrapped rotations; g73,k be the minimum signed axial gap in millimetres between N73’s locking face and the cover seat, positive for separation; and p74,k be N74 center displacement from its installed guide pose. For disjoint body sets A and B, clear(A,B) is the minimum signed surface separation over their collision shapes, positive when disjoint. The target alpha*=90 degrees. The adjustment work volume V is the closed cylinder coaxial with S, radius 45 mm, from 10 mm below the cover seat to 35 mm beyond the reset screw tip. A tool is outside V only when every point of every collision shape of that tool is outside V. A released measurement window is the latest 60 consecutive fresh 240 Hz post-physics samples, exactly 0.25 s, during which R∪T has no contact point with S∪N73. stable6 is true only at an open settled endpoint when |alpha−90|<=6 degrees and |dalpha/dt|<=2 degrees/s at every sample of that released window. A fresh lock certificate L is created only at an open settled endpoint when |alpha−90|<=3 degrees, g73<=0.5 mm, both nut-retention predicates hold, |thetaS,end−thetaS,start|<=1 degree across the released window, and stable6 is true. L records alphaL, thetaS_at_L and the certificate substep, allowing the jaws to close while maximum opening is temporarily unobservable. At every later substep L is revoked before cycle or score updates if H is true, either retention predicate fails, g73>0.5 mm, |thetaS−thetaS_at_L|>1 degree, R∪T contacts S∪N73, or adjustment motion occurs. Closure alone does not revoke L. Revocation clears all cycle records and clearance dwell. A cycle begins only with valid L when alpha crosses downward through 10 degrees. It completes only if the same uninterrupted L later crosses upward through 80 degrees and reaches a released settled endpoint lasting 48 consecutive fresh samples, exactly 0.20 s; ai is the angle at the last sample and L is then replaced by a newly recomputed certificate. Each cycle is the maximal interval between those crossings. Reversals, oscillations and repeated threshold crossings inside one interval cannot add cycles. Cycle records also clear on endpoint range over 2 degrees. C1 means at least one recorded cycle with |a1−90|<=3 degrees. C3 means three distinct recorded cycles, every |ai−90|<=3 degrees, and max(ai)−min(ai)<=2 degrees. Define fixture_work={cover,left jaw,right jaw,S,N73,N74,cold lever}. CLEAR is true only after C3 while D and W are wholly inside their respective rack cradles, clear(T,fixture_work)>=30 mm, clear(R,F∪M∪T∪Q)>=30 mm, both robot grippers are open, and all these predicates hold for 240 consecutive fresh 240 Hz samples, exactly 1.00 s. Eligibility is E25=stable6; E50=fresh valid L; E75=L∧C1∧(D outside V)∧(W outside V); E100=L∧C3∧CLEAR. After the final physics substep of every 20 Hz action, score=0 if H, otherwise max({0,0.25·1[E25],0.50·1[E50],0.75·1[E75],1.00·1[E100]}). The reported score is current, never a historical maximum. Reset clears H, pair-event state and work, previous motion samples, dwell counters, extrema, L and cycle records before the untouched settled state is sampled; that state must score exactly 0. Action 4800 executes all 12 native physics substeps, then its current score is evaluated once and returned as terminal score. Termination freezes all counters: no post-timeout physics, dwell advancement, certificate creation or score recovery occurs. Early termination uses the same current-score rule. Arm identity, safe action order, path, action count below the limit and physically valid alternative tool strategies do not enter the formula.

required_controls.name: control_untouched_initial_noop
required_controls.reason: The untouched settled maximum opening remains more than 6 degrees from 90 degrees with no inherited dwell, certificate or cycle history.

required_controls.name: control_angle_only_released_within_six
required_controls.reason: The released opening is within 6 degrees, but N73 remains unseated so no lock certificate exists.

required_controls.name: control_locked_within_three_no_cycle
required_controls.reason: A fresh released lock certificate exists within 3 degrees, but no physical cycle has completed.

required_controls.name: control_locked_one_cycle_tools_withdrawn
required_controls.reason: One retained cycle and both tools outside the adjustment volume qualify, but three cycles and final clearance dwell are absent.

required_controls.name: control_full_three_cycle_clear_dwell
required_controls.reason: The locked setting survives three valid cycles and the racked tools and open robot grippers remain clear for one fresh second.

required_controls.name: control_wrong_angle_locked
required_controls.reason: A safely locked 105 degree setting lies outside both grading bands.

required_controls.name: control_wrong_nut_seating
required_controls.reason: A released angle within 6 degrees earns angle credit, but a 2 mm N73 gap prevents certificate creation.

required_controls.name: control_unrestrained_locking_reaction
required_controls.reason: Starting from 90 degrees, zero-counterhold tightening continues until measured absolute setting drift is at least 6.01 degrees, leaving the released terminal angle outside the inclusive 6 degree band without invoking damage.

required_controls.name: control_postcycle_retention_drift
required_controls.reason: A controlled 4 degree screw drift revokes the lock certificate and clears cycles while a newly released endpoint remains within the 6 degree band.

required_controls.name: control_nut74_removed
required_controls.reason: N74 retention loss latches hard failure regardless of angle or prior progress.

required_controls.name: control_tool_drop_to_table
required_controls.reason: A qualifying unsupported 50 mm fall followed by impact latches deterministic tool-drop failure.

required_controls.name: control_fixture_displacement
required_controls.reason: Fixture translation over 10 mm latches hard failure and prevents scoring by moving the workpiece.

required_controls.name: control_energized_adjustment
required_controls.reason: Measured S or N73 motion above its explicit rate threshold while actuator force exceeds 1 N latches failure regardless of manipulating body or contact state.

required_controls.name: control_refinement_full_outcome
required_controls.reason: The independently executed safe full trajectory at 480 Hz must retain final score 1 and satisfy the declared angle and pair-force convergence checks.
